evidence: LangGraph-based resume optimization prototype with semantic skill matching, ATS scoring, metric preservation, and hallucination checks.
A compact, safety-first resume tailoring system built with LangGraph and Groq.
It parses a resume, extracts JD requirements, matches skills deterministically, rewrites the resume with an LLM, validates every claim and metric, and exports only when the output is safe.
Truth check catches invented claims before export
Regex-based metric preservation catches dropped numbers
Works across AI/ML, finance, business, marketing, design resumes
Every match, score, and validation decision is explainable
LLM used only where needed
Deterministic skill matching
Hallucination gate before export

LangGraph agentic workflow
Structured JSON I/O for all LLM calls
No domain-specific hardcoding
Load PDF/DOCX/TXT, validate inputs
LLM parses resume + analyzes JD into structured JSON
Deterministic skill matching, baseline ATS score
LLM rewrites resume with structured JSON prompt
Truth check, metric check, quality check
One targeted repair pass if validation fails
Exports only if all safety checks pass
Conditional routing: after validate, the graph decides autonomously — repair or export.
repair_done flag prevents infinite loops.
No embeddings. No ML models for matching. Pure deterministic Python:
Exact match — direct term or variant found in resume text
Token stem overlap — stemmed tokens of skill match stemmed tokens in evidence units
Fuzzy ratio — SequenceMatcher at ≥ 0.82 threshold
Acronym matching — ML matches Machine Learning, FastAPI matches via embedded acronym
Semantic aliases — vector databases matches if ChromaDB, Pinecone, or FAISS is present
All five tiers are explainable in an interview without referencing any model.
ATS = (matched/total × 50) + (required_matched/required_total × 35) + (evidence_quality × 15) − penalty
50% — overall keyword coverage
35% — required skills coverage (weighted higher)
15% — evidence quality (how strongly each skill appears

repo_analysis.problem: Detecting two classes in traffic footage: accident and non-accident.
features: Evaluates the model on a held-out test split
Runs video inference with a trained checkpoint
Provides an end-to-end pipeline for training, testing, and inference
evidence: AccidentVision is a YOLO-based traffic incident detection project.
The project detects two classes in traffic footage: accident, non-accident.
The notebook trains a YOLOv9e model, evaluates it on the held-out test split, and runs video inference with the trained checkpoint.
The notebook uses the following training setup: base model: yolov9e.pt, epochs: 25, image size: 250, batch size: 6, workers: 8, device: GPU 0.
The last recorded training epoch in the saved history reported the following metrics: precision: 0.78298, recall: 0.74298, mAP@0.50: 0.82092, mAP@0.50:0.95: 0.60247.

The notebook main.ipynb currently: Loads yolov9e.pt. Trains the model on the local dataset with the hyperparameters above. Loads the best checkpoint generated during training. Runs test-time validation and prints the final mAP@0.50. Runs video inference and saves annotated outputs locally.
The notebook is organized into three main parts: Training setup, Evaluation, Inference.

The repository includes the generated run artifacts again, mainly under: runs/detect/train1/ for the training curves, batch previews, and results.csv, runs/detect/val2/ for validation plots and predictions.json.
